title: First C-Walk Video
description: The first experience I had with learning to dance was C-Walking. At the time, I had discovered an online community of people on YouTube where people would share their practice on there, and I felt drawn since it seemed like a lot of asian diaspora people were doing this, so I watched tutorials and shared my own C-Walking videos

title: C-Walk crew tryout video
description: I joined an online crew called [N]erdiie [A]zn [C]lown [W]alkerz
notes: I guess this would be the first time I felt a sense of community and belonging through dance--in this case with an online community. I didn't really have this irl so that's probably what made it valuable for me at the time.

title: Imagine Music Festival 2018
description: This was my first time seeing shuffle dancers at a music festival and this moment kind of planted a seed in my mind of my desire to learn how to shuffle one day, so that at another festival, I could be in the crowd shuffling like the friends I made at this festival who inspired me, specifically my camping neighbors :)

title: Imagine Festival 2019
description: Acknowledged and further solidified my desire to learn shuffle dance for next music festival - I had planned to go to another festival in the spring of the next year, and I set a goal for myself that I would join a shuffle circle there. It was supposed to be at Ubbi Dubbi in Texas, which eventually got canceled because of covid, which also then led me to continue to learn shuffling anyways because of the pandemic. :)

title: First shuffle challenge: shuffle fitness
description: Participating in this shuffle challenge is what I consider the true start to my shuffle dance journey, since it was the point in time where I was in a mindset where I was intentionally learning and practicing the dance in a consistent way. In this challenge, the moderators of an Instagram account would post a move/combo each day, and the challenge was for the participants to learn from the tutorials they provided, and post on their own Instagram story

title: Posted first shuffle reel
description: Inspired by a reel Sterling Torres posted and I learned a flow/combo she did to 'On Your Mind' by Kaskade

title: First injury, sprained ankle
description: The first time I had an injury that had affected me greatly because of how it relates to myself and dancing was a sprained ankle - had a misstep walking down the stairs at Weimar Hbf after coming back from a trip to Berlin.
notes: This was the first moment I think I can remember my mental health being negatively affected because of dance -- or maybe rather the lack of it in this context. Maybe not only because I'd gotten the dopamine from the physical practice itself, but also possibly because of the dopamine hits from the affirmations online, since I was primarily connecting with other dancers online.

title: First (online) tournament participation: WSC
description: Prelims: https://www.instagram.com/p/CVUySkbM2Wa/ Round 1: https://www.instagram.com/p/CV-pxNng05F/ Made it past prelims, lost in round 1 to alvaro

title: First time participating in a music video!
description: Anna invited me to be a background dancer in Mark Dekoda's music video for Rave Harder Techno Bass! We went to EXIL outside of its opening hours and shot some clips, and also we were having our own seshes for fun and filming vids.
notes: This was one of my highlights of my time in Vienna, where I connected with other shufflers in real life for the first time.

title: Second (online) tournament participation: WSC
description: Prelims: https://www.instagram.com/reel/Ci8GQGeIDkc/ Round 1: https://www.instagram.com/reel/Ckbc54yoAzy/ “Made it past prelims, lost in round 1 to Marcel/Lotus”

title: First experience watching a dance battle in person
description: An aha moment on what it's like to experience these types of community events and that I love them. Validating moments when I would join dance circles, and people would dap me up afterwards, giving me respect about my flow

title: TSL Trip 2023
description: “Beginning of a core shuffle-identity crisis of mine: which country do I represent at competitions? Marbiik filmed clips of each country's shufflers, and they'd done the US one without me, and I appeared in the French and German/Swiss ones, fueled/incepted the identity crisis in a way”

title: First paid collab! Music video with irredrecords
description: Validating experience for someone to reach out to me, thinking that they'd want my dancing as a part of something. Lui and Mohammed helped film me at different spots in the city for the clip.

title: Riot of Rhythm Tournament 2023
description:
Made it into the bracket - didn't make it past the 1st round (against Infinity)

Matchups were made by participants choosing their opponents

title: Summer Shuffle Cup 2023
description: Made it into the bracket! - Didn't make it past the 1st round against Działo

title: TSL 2024
description: (Written on 01.03.2025) I know while I was there and experiencing it, it felt different but I wasn't sure why - I think for sure because of my health situations - but maybe as an extension this break I had for health kind of distanced me from my relationship with dance and led me to experience the event differently. Also my sense of belonging felt definitely weirder than the year before. In 2023 I wasn't called to be a part of the videos they were filming for the US shufflers, but I was a part of the French & German ones, and this year I didn't feel so connected with the US crowd too - they'd hype each other up, and I felt urges to run over and join but held myself back because to some extent I didn't feel a part of their community, and though I felt this trip was great in terms of me feeling closer with the German community, to some extent I wasn't sure how much I was a part of it either... Maybe the world cup concept doesn't fit for me? Where people are categorized by country

title: First US Battle: TC Battles
description:
Accomplishment! Made it past the first round, something I hadn't accomplished yet in previous battles. A shuffler who I enjoy watching said she liked my style. No qualification rounds, it was a first come first serve into the 32-person bracket. Interesting thing about this battle was that there was no limit to how long someone's round would be - you could dance as long as you wanted for your round. 

Round 1 vs OzzyModo
Round 2 vs Krisis

title: First Janeiro on spin
description: I got my first Janeiro on spin pole :) was just for a couple of seconds, felt great though, didn't know what to transition to afterwards

title: First Flying Pole Class
description:
Lea encouraged me to try out her flying pole class since I was progressing well in her handstand handspring class so I tried it out :)

Practiced entries, handsprings and getting used to the spinning in general
notes: Loved it!! I feel like trying this out is inner child healing work kind of, since freshman year in high school I'd always been curious about the cirque program at school, especially aerial silks, but didn't have the courage to try it out. Really fulfilling :)

title: First handspring!!
description:
Class with Mary

Got my first handspring(s) without needing a spot 🥹
notes:
was both in cup and twisted grip :D felt super nice that I could get this advanced trick 6 months into my pole practice. 

the wrist strength I'd built from bouldering for sure helped get me there

title: First House Dance Class
description: Joined Thuy & friends to a class Sharxilla was teaching. Don't remember what type of class but it was probably fundamentals or something like that
notes: Looking back on it now, going to classes with other dance friends (in this context shuffle friends) was a way that made me feel at home and part of a community in Paris, contributed to my sense of belonging 😌

title: First pole class (Absolute Beginner's)
description: Took my first pole class -- the fact that it was called "Introduction to the Pole Dance life..New members Absolute Beginner's" and that a man was the instructor all contributed to me feeling comfortable enough to try it out. I think we did basic spins and climbs.
notes:
The start of a new dance practice after some time of feeling a bit disconnected with my "main" one (shuffling)

The videos I watched a while back of boulderers trying pole dance and pole dancers trying bouldering definitely influenced my decision to try this out. Great decision and added so much to my life in Berlin and appreciation and awareness of my body and its capabilities :)

title: First video after people irl knowing I dance
description: The general story was that there was some drama on the school bus between friends and I felt guilty to one of my friends because of how I acted. So, I went home, filmed a video of me dancing to "Nothing Left of Me" by Wisnu and sent it to the friend as an apology. She was happy with it and forgave me.
notes: This is probably the first time where I consciously used dance as a method to regulate myself emotionally. Also, this was after a point where friends of mine had found out about my YouTube channel. Until a certain point I had only shared the dance part of my life with the online community I was a part of.

title: First time showing my face in a dance video
description: Made myself fully seen dancing online. Before that point I'd only shared videos without, which was relatively common back then in c-walk videos on YouTube
notes: I probably had gained some confidence after friends found out about my channel and showed their support, liking the dancing and content :)

title: Attended pole open mic for the first time
description: Came because a friend from my intermediate class at Boogaloo was performing and it turned out another friend (from handstand/handspring Thursday class) was also performing!!
notes:
It was super inspiring to watch people from different levels feel so comfortable with the group and space, and share their unique styles <3 felt like a super supportive and safe space and made me curious about trying to join in a future open mic maybe. 

Also it felt really heartwarming seeing other Asians performing, they were amazing and badass

reflections.text:
Especially with recent news about Xhufflis having had inappropriate communications with female minors in the community, and also I recently saw Lianet post on her story about women in the scene, I remembered this talk that Shuffle Well-Being hosted to talk about women in the battle scene in Europe.

I'd already for some time felt a bit disconnected from the scene for several reasons, but attending this talk was nice to hear how others also have been feeling a bit estranged--I felt connected with those sharing their thoughts, as I often do as a gay man in a cis male dominated & heternormative space.

I especially remember this mention of certain styles "naturally leaning" more feminine and masculine in their energies, and Théo coming up to me that he felt seen in what I'd commented, bringing up how he thinks it's cool that I'm also dabbling in pole dance which is female dominant, and that he agreed with me that having a gender binary framework on dance and dance styles can be limiting to dancers and the community.

title: Weekly Contemporary Classes :))
description: First time trying out contemporary 😄 It was a class taught by someone who does/studies/teaches dance pedagogy in Leipzig if I remember correctly. It was in the room next to the one where the hip hop classes were. Big open space.
notes:
I really enjoyed this class. I think I'd always been drawn to contemporary because of the kind of fluid motions and how flowy it seemed from what I'd seen watching So You Think You Can Dance growing up. I like that it shared elements with Ballet but expressed it a bit differently aesthetically. 

I remember being someone surprised or proud of myelf for picking up on the choreos the teacher would prepare relatively well. The warmups and exercises that had us traveling around the space and extending our bodies I remember were something I enjoyed.

title: "How to Dance Ballet" class by Marcelino, first time trying Ballet 🪰
description: A friend I met via the Ballroom community, Marcelino, who's a soloist at the Leipzig Ballet, taught an intro class for the community.
notes:
I felt very comfortable because of who was teaching it and who the class was for, it felt super safe to try something I was probably scared to as a young boy.

It felt great using strength, grace and clean lines at the same time.

title: HCI & Dance Research Internship for Master's Thesis
description: I moved to Paris because of an opportunity to intern under Sarah Fdili Alaoui and to take on an HCI project for my thesis which would involve dancers as users, participants & co-designers throughout the research process.
notes:
Lots of different feelings:
- Excitement because I'd be able to intertwine my academic journey with dance, something I'd been especially passionate about since moving to Europe
- A newfound sense of belonging through interests because of the dance communities the project and city would enable me be exposed to
- A somewhat mixed sense of resentment and apathy when life lows would come while work was intertwining and associating with a hobby that was used as a means of emotional/nervous system regulation

title: Got an email about a Dance x HCI internship opportunity (that could lead to theses)
description:
Was checking in my emails at the end of a trip to Milan with my friend group from Erasmus and found this email from Eva about an internship opportunity in Paris about designing tangibles for dance(r) research: "Designing tangible interactions to record movement" (March 2022 - August 2022)

"Dance is an embodied practice that is challenging to capture, document and archive because dance movement encompasses complex somatic and also cultural knowledge. Up to date, dance is mainly recorded through audio visual media on either institutional databases or streaming websites such as YouTube or Vimeo. However, mere video recordings do not inform on the cultural context, the movement qualities nor the kinesthetic sensations in dance, among others.
The goal of this internship is to go beyond visual and sonic interactions for dance archiving.

CONTEXT
Supervision: Sarah Fdili Alaoui
Lab: Exsitu Team, LISN, Université Paris-Saclay, CNRS,Orsay
https://ex-situ.lri.fr
Dates: Starts March 2022- August 2022 (6 months).
Net Monthly Salary: 500 € approx

OBJECTIVES
To design interactive wearable applications that allow dance artists to trace, capture and share their dance practices from their first-person perspective.
To deploy the technology in real-world situations.

REQUIRED SKILLS
We are looking for passionate candidates with good Design skills, and a strong background in one or several of the following domains: HCI, body-based interactions and movement and computing, humanities or dance."
notes: I hadn't known extensively about this field of HCI research, so somewhat randomly getting an email from my master's program director about this opportunity really excited me and motivated me about future opportunities, especially with potentiality of a career in academia.

title: First pole injury & first stitches
description:
I took a Beginner's Experts class at Boogaloo with Louise and, as my friend Elysse described it, "hubris got me" 🥲 There were people in the class above my level and I was trying to keep up.

I was attempting an Iguana to Archer transition and I fell on my face on the dismount (after achieving the shape to be fair hahah). 

I got cut between my right eyebrow and eye.
notes:
It was a good lesson to be honest about my skills and to take things slowly, to what my body is capable of in the moment, and that I shouldn't compare myself with other people's abilities and progress.

The moment itself wasn't so bad and didn't hurt so much, I was just annoyed I couldn't do much activity while I was recovering. 

Reflecting back though I recovered relatively quick and went for another class the day after I got my stitches out ahaha

title: Prague trip for Battle of Europe '25
description:
First time attending this battle, the previous time I wanted to I ended up staying in Vienna to spend time with friends I hadn't seen for a while.

Was staying at a hostel myself w/o other shuffle people.

Didn't make it past the preselection.

title: Riot of Rhythm 2025
description: Didn't make it past the preselection. Saw that my name was originally going into the bracket then it got crossed out
notes: this moment really dysregulated and triggered me and probably exacerbated the already negative feelings that had been brewing with how I associate myself with shuffling especially while living in Germany/Berlin

title: Dandayamana Janushirasana: got my elbows to my calves!
description:
aka standing head to knee

I got my elbows to my shin for the first time and looked down!! I think it was only on my left side
notes:
This asana isn't one of my favorites of the standing sequence and so when I reached this part of the progression I felt quite proud of my progression.

I've been taking a flexibility class weekly for the past month so I think it's been helping, especially for my hip flexor strength & mobility

title: First deadlift 💪🏼
description: Got my first deadlifts in class with Lea!!
notes: really proud of myself that I've built the strength relatively quickly to start to be able to do this, especially because it opens doors to lots of more advanced tricks and skills

title: First phoenixes 🐦‍🔥💫
description: From class with Laura: she subbed once before and I told her I really wanted to learn how to do phoenix and for this class she was teaching it :))
notes:
Felt so good, was rewatching the video so many times. Gotta keep practicing it and getting used to spinning around on static.

That deadlift training definitely helped for this since it's basically an aerial deadlift at the end of the movement.

title: First air walk to deadlift/handspring 🧚🏼‍♂️
description: Finally got twisted grip air walk to deadlift!! I had recently started trying out intermediate classes
notes: The queue to walk outward (like towards 2 o'clock) helped a lot

title: Trip to Cologne for Sterling's workshop
description:
Had a Deutschland-ticket adventure from Weimar to Cologne since Sterling Torres was giving a workshop at @flowfactorycgn

Learned and filmed a choreo at the workshop, connected with Maike from Wuppertal and then joined a meetup where we seshed and filmed a short choreo. Overall was a cute trip

title: Joined BassCaptives
description: Joined Francis Vo's international Melbourne Shuffle crew
notes:
An honor especially since Francis is an OG

Sadly not much had come really from this, I think I really thrive better from in person community feelings more honestly
